young-ahmed-2019.gazette: The Dardenne brothers shot again in the Meuse valley towns they have worked in since the 1990s, with an untrained teenage lead and a camera carried at his shoulder. The juvenile centre, the caseworkers, the farm placement are the Belgian institutions a boy in that position would actually pass through. Most of the film is framed at the height of someone walking away from you.

never-rarely-sometimes-always-2020.gazette: Hittman cast Sidney Flanigan, a Buffalo musician with no acting credits, and shot on 16mm in rural Pennsylvania and around the Port Authority terminal. The scene that gives the film its title is built from a clinic intake questionnaire read aloud, held in one unbroken take on the actor's face. Pennsylvania's parental-consent law is not a plot device; it is why the bus is in the movie.

the-old-oak-2023.gazette: Filming in County Durham pit villages where the collieries closed a generation ago, Loach cast locals — his lead had spent his working life as a firefighter and a union official — alongside Syrian families resettled in the North East after 2016. He shoots in sequence and releases the script a scene at a time, so the actors learn what happens when the characters do. It was announced as his last film.
the-old-oak-2023.prism: The realism cuts both ways: a village that has been photographed as a symptom for forty years finally gets to talk, and it talks in the vocabulary of a strike it lost. Solidarity here isn't an ideal being proposed, it's the last surviving piece of infrastructure.

anora-2024.gazette: Anora was shot on 35mm in Brighton Beach and south Brooklyn, with the neighborhood and the clubs themselves filling out the frame around Mikey Madison. Sex workers consulted on the script and on set, down to how a shift is worked and what gets said in a back room. The mansion, the jet and the ring are the only things in the film that behave like a fairy tale.

before-midnight-2013.gazette: Linklater, Hawke and Delpy wrote the third film together, nine years after the second, and shot it in the southern Peloponnese over a matter of weeks. The drive from the airport runs unbroken for more than ten minutes; the hotel-room fight is staged to play close to real time. By then the actors had spent eighteen years being the same two people.

bridge-of-spies-2015.gazette: Donovan published his own account of the Abel case in 1964, and the film works from it, from the trial record, and from the Supreme Court appeal a Brooklyn insurance lawyer argued and lost. The exchange it builds toward took place on the morning of 10 February 1962, and the production filmed on the Glienicke Bridge itself. Frederic Pryor, the student handed over at Checkpoint Charlie in the same hour, was alive to see the film released.
bridge-of-spies-2015.prism: The tidiness is the tell: two prisoners released at two points in a divided city, timed to the same hour, is the choreography a state uses when it wants the deal without admitting there was one. Donovan's famous argument for sparing Abel was pragmatic — a live spy is tradeable — and the film has to work to make that land as principle.

faces-places-2017.gazette: Varda was 88 and JR was 33 when they drove a truck that prints photographs the size of a house wall across working France. In a half-demolished miners' row in the north they pasted the last remaining tenant onto the front of her own condemned home; on the Normandy coast, a portrait glued to a fallen bunker was gone with the next tide. The mines had closed decades before either photograph was taken.

the-trial-of-the-chicago-7-2020.gazette: The transcript of the 1969 conspiracy trial runs to thousands of pages and is public; Sorkin worked from it and then compressed — timelines telescoped, speeches merged, a closing scene the record does not contain. Bobby Seale, bound and gagged at the defense table on Judge Julius Hoffman's order, required no dramatizing at all. Every conviction was reversed on appeal in 1972.

judas-and-the-black-messiah-2021.gazette: William O'Neal gave the FBI a floor plan of the apartment at 2337 West Monroe; officers fired into it before dawn on 4 December 1969, and Fred Hampton, 21, died in his bed. O'Neal later sat for the only interview he ever gave, for Eyes on the Prize, and the film cuts straight to the tape. He killed himself the night it was broadcast, in January 1990.
judas-and-the-black-messiah-2021.prism: The title does the same work the files do: O'Neal was a teenager when the Bureau turned him with a car-theft charge, which makes betrayal a strange word for something an agency engineered and paid for. And the only reason anyone can name the floor plan is that the government wrote it down and was later forced to hand it over.

argentina-1985-2022.gazette: The Trial of the Juntas opened in Buenos Aires in April 1985, less than two years after the dictatorship ended, before a civilian court while the generals still commanded loyalty in the barracks. Strassera and a team of lawyers young enough to be uncompromised built the case out of survivor testimony and the CONADEP report published the year before. His closing words — nunca más — were already the title of that report.

holy-spider-2022.gazette: Saeed Hanaei killed sixteen women in Mashhad between 2000 and 2001, in a city built around a shrine, and told reporters he was cleaning the streets. He was hanged in 2002; by then part of the press and part of the public had treated him as a man doing necessary work, and his son said on camera that he would carry it on. None of it could be filmed in Iran, so Mashhad was rebuilt in Jordan.

saint-omer-2022.gazette: Alice Diop sat in the courtroom at Saint-Omer in 2016 for the trial of a woman who had left her fifteen-month-old daughter on the beach at Berck-sur-Mer to the incoming tide. Long stretches of the testimony in the film are the words spoken there, transcribed and delivered straight to a fixed camera. Diop was pregnant while she took the notes.
saint-omer-2022.prism: Verbatim is not neutral: a court transcript has already decided which questions get asked, and the film keeps those questions, so what ends up on screen is a French legal proceeding's idea of what a Senegalese woman needs to explain. The camera doesn't fix that; it just refuses to cut away and leaves the room's assumptions sitting in frame.

12-12-the-day-2023.gazette: On the night of 12 December 1979, weeks after Park Chung-hee's assassination, a faction of Korean generals arrested the army chief of staff without authorization and held the capital by morning. The film changes the names — Chun Doo-hwan becomes Jeon Du-gwang — but keeps the chronology, the phone calls and the units that moved, most of it established in court a decade and a half later. It sold more than thirteen million tickets in a country of about fifty-one million people.

oppenheimer-2023.gazette: Nolan built the film on American Prometheus and on the 1954 security hearing, whose transcript the Atomic Energy Commission published at the time and released unredacted in 2014. The Trinity shot went off at 5:29 in the morning of 16 July 1945 in the New Mexico desert; the proceeding that stripped Oppenheimer's clearance was held in a temporary government building, not a courtroom, with his own wiretapped conversations in the hands of the other side. The Energy Department formally vacated that 1954 decision in December 2022, seven months before the film opened.

the-seed-of-the-sacred-fig-2024.gazette: Rasoulof shot the film clandestinely in Iran and cut real phone video from the 2022 protests into it — footage recorded on the street by ordinary people after Mahsa Amini died in custody. In May 2024 he was sentenced to eight years and flogging; he left the country on foot and reached Germany in time for the Cannes premiere. Members of the cast stayed behind.
the-seed-of-the-sacred-fig-2024.prism: Documentary contraband is the right description: the protest clips aren't illustration, they're evidence a state worked to make unshowable, and wrapping them in fiction is how they got across the border. The cost is legible in the credits — a film smuggled out is also a list of people who can still be found.
